editor_note: The six rewritten entries (9, 44, 65, 67-69) are faithful and read naturally, with no drift: the integer-bounds caveat and error code 4710 survive intact ("entera con un límite inferior y superior explícitos"), the postprocessing mapping and default 3 are preserved ("el valor predeterminado no cambia y sigue siendo `3`"), and the None/4712 condition in circuit_metrics is unchanged.

Entry 28 (the Table 1 caption) means the same as the English. The causal clause "ya que solo se utiliza una ronda de QAOA con parámetros óptimos del circuito obtenidos en una CPU" keeps the reason, the "mínimo y casi constante" claim keeps its strength, and the reference back to the description section is still there. The one slip is consistency: the caption writes the problem name in lowercase as "problema market split", but the same page writes "Market Split" everywhere else (entries 24, 25, 29, 58, 62). It should be capitalized to match.

editor_note: I checked the three rewritten entries (40, 41, 44) for meaning first, then for naturalness. Their meaning is faithful: the 10% threshold, width 9 / 10 qubits, the 80–90% and ~15% figures, the width approaching 60, N = 50 / 51 qubits and the closing caveat all come through. The problem is that the rewrites don't match terms used on the rest of the page. They say 'cadena de bits oculta', but entries 25, 46 and 65 say 'bitstring oculto'. Entry 44 also says 'en un solo trabajo' where entry 38 says 'en un solo job'. Separately, entry 44 has two calques: 'Para preservar el tiempo de QPU' (more natural: 'Para ahorrar tiempo de QPU') and 'informa los recuentos de shots' (more natural: 'muestra los recuentos de shots').

examples.translation: a medida que crece el ancho de la cadena de bits oculta
examples.suggested: a medida que crece el ancho del bitstring oculto
examples.why: Entries 25, 46 and 65 say 'bitstring oculto'. Switching to 'cadena de bits oculta' here and in entry 44 means the same concept is called two different things on one page.

examples.source: To preserve QPU time, ... the executable example below reports shot counts
examples.translation: Para preservar el tiempo de QPU, ... el ejemplo ejecutable que sigue informa los recuentos de shots
examples.suggested: Para ahorrar tiempo de QPU, ... el ejemplo ejecutable que sigue muestra los recuentos de shots
examples.why: 'preservar el tiempo' and 'informa los recuentos' are literal calques of the English. A native technical writer would use 'ahorrar' and 'muestra'.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful. Entry 72 keeps the gate order and roles ("una puerta CNOT con Q como control y su propio qubit como objetivo, y luego aplica una puerta Hadamard a Q"), entry 73's math matches the English exactly, and its prose is a clean rendering ("agrupemos los términos anteriores según los resultados de las mediciones sobre los qubits A y Q").

Entries 53 and 87 are faithful and natural ("ajustar con precisión", "fija la opción `seed_transpiler`", "optimización binaria con restricciones", consistent "guía del Aqarios Constrained Quantum Optimizer"). In entry 78, "addressed by variable name" is rendered as "indicada por el nombre de la variable". That sounds as if the solution is identified by one variable's name, when the English means the solution's values are looked up by variable name. It does not mislead in any serious way, but a native editor would write "indexada por nombre de variable". The rest of entry 78 (degenerate optima, `solution_bitstrings`, character position) is accurate.

examples.source: Only the first solution is considered here, addressed by variable name.
examples.translation: Aquí solo se considera la primera solución, indicada por el nombre de la variable.
examples.suggested: Aquí solo se considera la primera solución, indexada por nombre de variable.
examples.why: 'indicada por' does not convey 'addressed/accessed by'. It reads as if one variable's name identifies the solution, not that the solution's values are keyed by variable names.

editor_note: Entry 60 says the same thing as the English and would not mislead a learner. "Evalúa la fidelidad de proceso de QFT con Orbit" is accurate and reads naturally. The one problem is that the product name "Qiskit Function" is translated as "una función de Qiskit". House style keeps Qiskit Functions in English (ALWAYS_ENGLISH_NAMES), and entries 53, 54 and 57 on this page already do that ("Qiskit Functions de Q-CTRL"), so it should be "una Qiskit Function de Quantum Elements".

examples.source: Benchmark QFT process fidelity with Orbit, a Qiskit Function by Quantum Elements
examples.translation: Evalúa la fidelidad de proceso de QFT con Orbit, una función de Qiskit de Quantum Elements
examples.suggested: Evalúa la fidelidad de proceso de QFT con Orbit, una Qiskit Function de Quantum Elements
examples.why: Qiskit Functions is a product name that stays in English in every locale (ALWAYS_ENGLISH_NAMES), and entry 57 on this page already writes 'Qiskit Functions de Q-CTRL'. The translated form doesn't change the meaning, but it breaks house style and is inconsistent within the file.

editor_note: Rewritten entry 12 is faithful and reads naturally: frustration, the random positive/negative $J_{ij}$ ("intensidades de interacción"), the triangular-arrangement example and "frustration is compounded globally" → "esta frustración se agrava globalmente" all match the English, with nothing dropped or inverted.

None of the 23 rewritten entries changes the meaning. Conditions, quantities and caveats all match the English, including the O(n^2) vs O(n) argument in [17], the 60/300 PUB counts in [49] and the MEM caveat in [51]. Four things are still worth fixing. Entry [67] tells the reader to look in "la sección Setup", but that heading is rendered "Configuración" [29]. Within the rewritten entries, 'gate' is "compuertas" in [17]/[33] but "puertas" in [35], and 'transpiler' is "transpilador" in [33] but "transpiler" in [42]/[56]. Entry [33] renders 'raw' as "sin procesar" while every other entry uses "en bruto". In [46], "asistente de agrupación" is a calque for the code's grouping helper.
